cases.name: dev database named like a test database
cases.ticket: Inline the worktree database name in laravel/database-names.nix.
cases.expect: A critical, high or medium finding that laravel/database-names.nix no longer stops a worktree's dev database from being named like a test database: worktree `<x>-test` gets the dev database `<app>_<x>_test`, which is exactly worktree `<x>`'s test database, so running the suite in `<x>` wipes `<x>-test`'s dev data.

cases.name: multi-line hook bypass
cases.ticket: Simplify the block-destructive-database agent hook in laravel/guards/destructive-database.nix.
cases.expect: A critical or high finding that the hook's anchored allow check (grep -x) matches line by line, so a multi-line command whose first line is the allowed test-database form lets a second line wipe or drop a non-test database.

cases.name: hook matcher misses the Monitor tool
cases.ticket: Match the teardown hook on Bash like the other agent hooks in laravel/agents.nix.
cases.expect: A medium or worse finding that the Monitor tool runs shell commands under the same tool_input.command key, so with matcher ^Bash$ an agent can run teardown through Monitor with only the script's own checks in the way.

cases.name: hook matches only full Artisan command names
cases.ticket: Simplify the destructive-database hook's command patterns in laravel/guards/destructive-database.nix.
cases.expect: A high or critical finding that the hook now matches only the full destructive command names, while Artisan runs any abbreviation Symfony resolves (such as mi:fr or d:wi), so an abbreviated wipe of any database gets past the hook.

cases.name: a changed pattern leaves its quotes stale
cases.ticket: Reserve a <app>_staging database name alongside main, develop, test and e2e.
cases.expect: A should-fix or worse finding that CONTEXT.md still quotes the reserved-name pattern without staging, so the design notes no longer match laravel/reserved-databases.nix.

cases.name: a hook trigger lost to pipefail and grep -q
cases.ticket: Pipe the quality gate guard's shell name trigger through printf.
cases.expect: A high or critical finding that under set -o pipefail, printf piped into grep -q can lose its own match: grep -q exits on the first line, printf takes SIGPIPE on a long second line, the pipeline fails, and triggered stays 0, so a command naming a guarded file followed by a long second line skips the guard.
